merge_request.title: Add loud greeting mode to greet()

overview.what: The greet() function gains an optional loud flag that, when set, upper-cases the greeting message instead of returning it in normal case. A new test covers the loud path.
overview.why: To let callers request an emphatic/shouted greeting without changing the default behavior for existing callers.
overview.risks: No test exists for the default (non-loud) path after this change, so a regression in the base message format wouldn't be caught by this diff's new test alone — though the original behavior is unchanged and low-risk.
overview.out_of_scope: No CLI, API, or call-site changes are included — nothing in the codebase actually passes loud=True yet, and no input validation (e.g. non-bool loud) is added.

steps.title: Add loud parameter to greet()
steps.intro: The core change: greet() builds its message as before, then conditionally upper-cases it based on a new keyword argument.
steps.detail: greet(name) is extended with a defaulted loud=False parameter so existing call sites are unaffected. The message is now built into a local variable and conditionally transformed with .upper() before being returned, which is a minimal, backward-compatible way to add the feature.

files.why: Houses the greet() function being extended with the loud option.

steps.title: Add test for loud greeting
steps.intro: A new test file checks that passing loud=True produces an upper-cased greeting.
steps.detail: This is the first test file for the greeter module, added specifically to cover the new loud path. It doesn't include a case for the default/non-loud path, so it only verifies the new behavior rather than guarding the whole function.

files.why: New test asserting greet("Ada", loud=True) returns the upper-cased greeting.
watchpoints: No accompanying test for the default (loud=False) case in this new file.
